pride_data.title: Linear Protein Identification of Soluble and Insoluble Fractions from In-Situ DSSO Crosslinked Human Mitochondria
pride_data.projectDescription: In this project, freshly isolated mitochondria from K-562 cells were crosslinked immediately with the homobifunctional and membrane-permeable reagent disuccinimidyl sulfoxide (DSSO). The study focuses on the comprehensive identification of proteins, specifically distinguishing between soluble and insoluble fractions. Both fractions were digested using Trypsin and analyzed using Liquid Chromatography coupled with Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and Data-Dependent Acquisition (DDA) methods. The resulting data were processed using MaxQuant software.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: In this project, freshly isolated mitochondria were crosslinked with disuccinimidyl sulfoxide (DSSO). Lysed mitochondria were separated into a soluble proteome and an insoluble proteome. Protein digestion was performed followed by peptide purification using C18 cartridges, strong cation-exchange chromatography (SCX), and hydrophilic strong anion exchange (hSAX) chromatography in the second dimension. LC-MS/MS was performed and the resulting data were processed using MaxQuant software.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Obtained raw files from DDA runs were processed using MaxQuant, and the resulting files were used to evaluate protein abundances (iBAQ) in both soluble and insoluble fractions.
